rationale: JD3-CLOSURE regression. The analyzer's `method_definition` case read `scopeOwnerName(scopeStack) ?? containerOwnerName(node)`, and `scopeOwnerName` is a CLASS-SCOPE lookup — so inside a class body it answered for every object literal nested there, and the same construct gave two answers depending on where it was written: `class C { m() { const api = { run(){} } } }` published `contains C -> run` while the module-scope `const api = { run(){} }` published `contains api -> run`. Measured consequence: the 2 rows published for `svelte/src/legacy/legacy-client.js` (`new Proxy({}, { get(){}, has(){} })`) registered as UNEXPLAINED fabrications at confidence 1.0 on a 600-file svelte draw, because the oracle's nameability rule declines a literal it cannot bind. Three shapes are pinned so the fix cannot over-reach: a NAMED literal inside a class takes the literal's binding; an UNNAMED literal inside a class takes NO owner at all — a call argument names nothing, and a class is not a better answer than silence, which is what the module-scope path already did; and a real class member still belongs to its class.

expectSymbols.note: a literal with no binding: the symbol survives, its owner is the qualified carrier path and it gets NO containment edge

a `new Proxy({}, {…})` argument names nothing, so the enclosing class is not a better owner than silence — this row is the 1.0-confidence fabrication the oracle declines
